DaVita renal dietitian, Amity in Florida, works with her patients to find foods low in phosphorus, potassium and sodium. Here is a favorite that has been modified for the renal diet — Almost Mashed Potatoes. Enjoy this great taste and still maintain your kidney-friendly diet.
steps: Cut the cauliflower into pieces and rinse with water.
Place the cauliflower pieces in a microwave safe dish, cover and cook on high for 8 to 10 minutes or until soft.
Drain off moisture from the cooked cauliflower.
Carefully place the hot cauliflower in a blender and blend until smooth.
Add the cream cheese, garlic and pepper. Blend to combine ingredients.
Remove mixture from the blender and serve hot.
hints: One medium head cauliflower yields 6 cups.
Garlic powder may be substituted for the minced garlic.
Since cauliflower is bland like potatoes, this recipe tastes similar to mashed potatoes. The potassium content is 100 mg lower per serving.
To reduce fat content, use light cream cheese. Protein, sodium, potassium and phosphorus content will be slightly higher.

title: Creamy Fruit Salad
description: Enjoy kidney-friendly recipe Creamy Fruit Salad by Akemi from Nebraska. Fruits in the recipe can be substituted with any low potassium fruits of your choice, and if low sugar or no sugar is a must, substitute artificial sweetener.
ingredients: 15 ounces canned peaches in light syrup
steps: Cut apples, pears and peaches into bite-size pieces. Cut strawberries into quarters.
Place cut fruit in a large bowl. Set aside.
Place a metal bowl and metal beaters of a hand mixer in the freezer for 15 to 30 minutes. Pour heavy cream into the bowl and mix with chilled beaters until stiff peaks form.
In a medium bowl, mix cream cheese, sugar, and sour cream until smooth. Gently fold in whipped cream until mixed well.
Just before serving, pour cream cheese mixture over fruit and gently stir.
Top with fresh berries and serve.
hints: Substitute with any low potassium fruits of your choice. Make it colorful! (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries or a mixture).
This is my family’s favorite fruit salad recipe and a great potluck item. It’s best to eat it the same day because it can get watery overnight.
Reduce ingredients in half to make a smaller amount.

title: Apple Onion Omelet
description: Try this delicious recipe for Apple Onion Omelet by DaVita dietitian Brenda from Washington. She uses some of her favorite regional foods so you can create a delicious, dialysis-appropriate meal with splendid flavors from the Pacific Northwest.
steps: Preheat oven to 400º F.
Peel and core apple. Thinly slice apple and onion.
Beat eggs with milk, water and pepper in a small bowl; set aside.
Over medium heat, melt butter in a small, ovenproof skillet.
Add onion and apple to the skillet and sauté until onion becomes translucent, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Spread out the onion and apple mixture evenly in the skillet.

Pour egg mixture evenly into the skillet and cook over medium heat until the edges begin to set. Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the top. Transfer skillet to the oven and bake until the center is firmly set, approximately 10 to 12 minutes.
Cut omelet in half and slide each half onto an individual plate. Serve immediately.
hints: Walla Walla sweet onion recommend if available.
Jonagold, Gala or McIntosh are the best apple varieties for this recipe.

title: Garlic Herb Vinaigrette Dressing
description: Add a little zip to your kidney-friendly salad with this garlic herb vinaigrette dressing. This homemade dressing tastes better than anything you’ll buy off the shelf and you don’t have to worrying about sodium, phosphorus and potassium.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® original blend herb seasoning
steps: Place all ingredients into a jar with a tight lid and shake.
Ready to serve.
hints: Leftover dressing keeps well in the refrigerator for about 2 weeks.
Use dressing as a marinade for meat or vegetables.

title: High Protein Piña Colada
description: Learn how to make a tasty, high-protein Piña Colada with this easy recipe.
ingredients: 1 ounce Syntrax Nectar Whey Protein Isolate®, Caribbean Cooler
steps: Pour pineapple juice into the blender
Add the protein powder and blend until smooth
Add crushed ice and blend until smooth
Pour into serving glass
Add lemon lime soda or ginger ale
Garnish with small pineapple slices.
hints: Syntrax Nectar Whey Protein Isolate® may be purchased online or at The Vitamin Shoppe. One scoop or individual package equals 1 ounce and provides 23 grams protein.
Freeze the extra serving until ready to drink later.
Use ginger ale (regular or diet) instead of lemon-lime soda if desired.

title: Brunch Nachos
description: Egg and turkey bacon are added to traditional nacho ingredients to create Brunch Nachos, a tasty Mexican dish for your next breakfast or brunch.
ingredients: 4 ounces unsalted large size tortilla chips (about 30 chips)
1 small green bell pepper (or orange, red)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Cut bell pepper into thin strips. Dice red onion. Chop tomatoes and cilantro. Cut turkey bacon into small pieces.
To make pico de gallo, combine chopped tomato, onion and cilantro in a small bowl. Squeeze juice from one lime on top and stir.
To make crema, place sour cream in a bowl and add juice of one lime. Whisk together and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place tortilla chips in one layer on baking sheet. Top chips with dried seasonings, bell pepper and shredded cheese.
Bake in oven for 12 minutes.
While chips are baking, heat a non-stick pan over high heat. Crack eggs into a bowl, whisk and scramble in pan; set aside.
Remove chips from the oven and top with scrambled egg, chopped turkey bacon, pico de gallo, drizzle of crema and additional sprinkle of cilantro. Enjoy!
hints: Elyse chooses Garden of Eatin’® unsalted corn chips.
This nachos recipe is perfect for a breakfast brunch.
For more heat, substitute Monterey jack pepper cheese for cheddar cheese.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
description: Jamaican Jerk Chicken is a Caribbean-style grill-roasted chicken marinated a fiery hot combination of jerk spices and seasonings that include ginger, cloves, allspice, nutmeg, cinnamon, black pepper, hot chilies and a touch of brown sugar for sweetness.
ingredients: 2 habanero or 1 scotch bonnet chili pepper
steps: Coarsely chop the green and yellow onions. Peel and chop the ginger. Mince the garlic cloves. Seed and chop the hot peppers.
Place all ingredients, except chicken, in a food processor and process until smooth.
Place chicken and blended mixture in a dish or large zip-top bag. Seal and refrigerate to marinate for 3 to 24 hours.
Remove chicken from the container and discard remaining marinade.
Heat a grill on medium-high heat. Oil the grill rack, then add chicken and cook on each side for about 10 to 12 minutes. Chicken should reach 165° F before removing from the grill.
hints: Use a grill pan if grill is not available to get char marks on chicken.
If habanera and scotch bonnet peppers are unavailable substitute with your favorite hot chili.

title: Flourless Pumpkin Muffins
description: DaVita dietitian Alissa created a protein-packed pumpkin muffin without flour to share with her dialysis patients. The secret is a combination of peanut butter, eggs and baking soda.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line muffin tin with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, combine all ingredients except chocolate chips, mixing until smooth. Fold in chocolate chips.
Distribute batter evenly into 12 muffins.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, until centers are firm and starting to crack. Cool for 15 minutes and enjoy.
hints: If you prefer use reduced-fat peanut butter. This change adds approximately 5 grams of carbohydrate and lowers fat by 3 grams per serving.
These muffins are a tasty way to add extra protein in a snack or meal.
Peanut butter adds more potassium and phosphorus but is a great source of protein. Ask your dietitian if you need to add a phosphate binder when you eat this muffin for a snack.

title: Peach Crisp
description: Juicy Georgia peaches make an irresistible dessert in this kidney-friendly recipe for Peach Crisp. Enjoy it right from the oven when the fruit is warm and the topping extra crisp.
ingredients: 4 cups fresh peaches, peeled, pitted and sliced
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F. Spray a 9” x 9” baking dish with nonstick spray.
Mix peaches with lemon juice and granulated sugar or Splenda® granular sweetener. Pour into baking dish.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, nutmeg and cinnamon in a bowl. Cut in margarine with pastry blender or two knives until mixture is crumbly. Sprinkle over peaches.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until fruit is soft and crumbs are brown. Serve warm or at room temperature. Garnish with two tablespoons nondairy whipped topping and a mint leaf.
hints: If fresh peaches are unavailable, use canned or frozen sliced peaches.
2 medium peaches yield approximately 1 cup when peeled and sliced.
If made with Splenda No Calorie Sweetener granular and Splenda brown sugar blend, calories decrease to 247 and 32 g carbohydrate. Count as 2 carbohydrate choices.

title: Chicken Fajitas with Pineapple Salsa
description: Chicken Fajitas with Pineapple Salsa adds a burst of pinapple flavor to a tasty Mexican dish. This spicy meal is a treat for the whole family and recommended on a kidney-friendly diet.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Pineapple Salsa (see recipe under Sauces and Seasonings)
steps: Preheat oven to 300° F. Wrap tortillas in foil; heat in oven for 10 minutes.
Cut chicken breats into 1″ strips.
Place oil in nonstick frying pan over medium heat; add chicken, seasonings and lemon juice. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add peppers and onion to frying pan; cook for 3 to 5 minutes more or until chicken is no longer pink and juice run clear. Add cilantro to chicken mixture.
Divide chicken mixture between tortillas; fold tortillas over. Serve each with 1 tablespoon of pineapple salsa.
hints: One serving makes a complete meal.
Nutritional information is for 2 fajitas plus 2 tablespoons pineapples salsa.
Adjust the amount of chicken to match your meal plan for a lower or higher protein diet.

title: Tasty Chicken Patties
description: DaVita renal dietitian Melanie from Ohio shares her recipe for kidney-friendly Tasty Chicken Patties, an excellent alternative to salmon or tuna patties for the person who’s following the dialysis diet but doesn’t care for fish.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften.
Using a fork, mash chicken with juices in a medium bowl.
Add the cream cheese, egg, sage, garlic powder, black pepper, onion powder, Italian seasoning and bread crumbs; mix well.
Form six patties.
In a medium skillet heat olive oil over medium heat.
Fry patties for 5- to 6 minutes on each side or until crispy on the outside and heated through.
hints: Choose the canned chicken lowest in sodium.Melanie uses Keystone Chicken (available at Walmart).
Chicken Patties are very similar to salmon or tuna patties, but might be better liked by someone who doesn’t care for fish.

Look for Kikkoman brand panko bread crumbs– the sodium content is lower compared to commercial and generic unseasoned bread crumbs. Unsalted or low-sodium crushed saltines are an acceptable alternative to the bread crumbs.
Variations: instead of patties, form into 24 chicken meatballs. Meatballs could be eaten as a high-protein snack or used with theDaVita.com Roasted Red Pepper Sauce recipe over pasta.

title: Ginger-Apple Sparkler
description: Ginger-Apple Sparkler is a unique kidney-friendly recipe for your next big party.
ingredients: 1 six-inch piece fresh ginger, finely diced
steps: To prepare ginger syrup, place sugar*, grater ginger and water in a medium saucepan; bring to boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour until ginger flavor is strong. Strain mixture and refrigerate to chill.
To prepare Ginger-Apple Sparkler, place one tablespoon ginger syrup in each glass (use short tumblers).
Fill with ice cubes, pour in 1/2-cup cider and stir to combine.
Garnish with cinnamon stick and crystallized ginger.
hints: Syrup may be stored in the refrigerator up to 2 weeks.
Ginger is often used to help treat nausea and motion sickness.

*For those with diabetes, omit the sugar in ginger syrup. Instead, make concentrated ginger-flavored water. Sweeten to taste with sugar substitute. Nutrients decrease to 61 calories, 15 grams carbohydrate.

title: Bavarian Apple Tart
description: Bavarian Apple Tart is a creamy, cinnamon accented baked treat that will make your kitchen smell as mouthwatering as an Alpine village bakery. DaVita renal dietitian Gertrude from Colorado made a few kidney-friendly modifications and now her fiend’s Bavarian Apple Tart is low in sodium. potassium and phosphorus and suitable for a dialysis diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Set cream cheese out to soften. Peel, core and slice apples.
Cream together butter, 1/3 cup sugar and 1/4 teaspoon vanilla.
Fold in flour to make a dough.
Spread dough on bottom and sides of a 9″ spring form pan.
In a medium bowl combine softened cream cheese and 1/3 cup sugar; mix well.
Add egg and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla; mix until blended.
Pour mixture into pastry-lined pan.
Combine 1/3 cup sugar and cinnamon; toss with apples until all are coated.
Spoon apple mixture over cream cheese layer.
Sprinkle with almonds.
Bake at 450° F for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 400° F and continue baking for 25 minutes. Cool.
hints: One medium apple yields 1 cup when peeled and cored.
You can substitute fresh cranberries for slivered almonds on top of tart to reduce phosphorus to 53 mg per serving.
For a lower carbohydrate version diabetics can substitute Splenda® granular instead of sugar; carbohydrate is reduced to 19 grams, calories 266.

title: Chocolate Smoothie
description: Chocolate Smoothie is a creamy treat for people with diabetes who are on dialysis. It features egg whites, which can be a great substitute for other proteins. Try this delicious kidney-friendly recipe today.
steps: Combine cocoa, cold water and sugar.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add egg whites and 3 tablespoons of the whipped topping. Mix until whipped topping melts completely.
Top with 1 tablespoon whipped topping and chocolate bar shavings.
hints: Pasteurized egg whites are safe to consume without cooking.
Add 1/4 teaspoon mint extract for a chocolate mint smoothie.
People with diabetes can substitute sugar substitute if desired. Carbohydrate is reduced to 6 grams per serving.

title: Lively Lime Shrimp
description: This kidney-friendly recipe for Lively Lime Shrimp adds a burst of flavor with every bite.
steps: Chop onion and cilantro. Mince chili, garlic and bell pepper. Thinly slice cucumber.
Peel and devein shrimp.
For dressing, stir together lime juice, green onion, cilantro, jalapeno, oil, garlic and salt in a medium bowl.
In a separate medium size bowl, toss shrimp with 2 tablespoons of the dressing to marinade. Reserve remaining dressing. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat broiler. Remove shrimp from marinade and broil 3-inches from the heat source for 1-1/2 minutes per side or until opaque.
Remove from broiler and immediately toss hot shrimp with reserved dressing and red bell pepper. Cool to room temperature.
Arrange shrimp on cucumber slices and serve.
hints: Barbecue shrimp on a grill instead of broiling if desired.

title: Lemon Flavored Couscous with Zucchini
description: DaVita renal dietitian Martha from Missouri created Lemon Flavored Couscous with Zucchini by adjusting her couscous salad recipe ingredients and adding heat to make a satisfying healthy dish for the kidney diet.
steps: Chop celery, onion and parsley. Quarter and slice zucchini.
In a sauce pan, combine the water and 1 tablespoon of the oil and bring to a boil. Stir in couscous and cover. Remove from heat; let stand 5 minutes.
Combine lemon juice with zest, cayenne pepper and cumin.
In a large skillet, heat remaining 1 tablespoon of canola oil over medium heat and sauté celery, onion and zucchini until softened.
Transfer into a large serving dish and mix together the cooked couscous, the vegetables, cranberries, parsley, lemon juice and seasonings. Fluff with fork before serving. Serve hot.
hints: Mix lemon juice and seasonings together before adding to couscous.
Crookneck squash or other varieties of summer squash can be substituted for zucchini.

title: Frozen Sugar Cookie Sandwiches
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Rachel from Illinois, whipped up a delicious kidney-friendly dessert recipe — Frozen Sugar Cookie Sandwiches. Frosty and sweet whipped topping is sandwiched between two tasty sugar cookies…yum!
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Splenda® No Calorie granular sweetener
3 cups Reddi-Wip® Fat Free Dairy whipped topping
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Set butter and cream cheese out to soften.
In a medium bowl, mix flour, baking soda, and baking powder. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream together butter and Splenda until smooth. Beat in egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Gradually blend in dry ingredients.
Form teaspoons of dough into balls, and place on ungreased cookie sheet. Flatten the dough ball by pressing down with the bottom of a glass.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, or until golden. Remove from oven and let stand until completely cool.
With a mixer beat cream cheese, sugar and the remaining vanilla extract. Gently fold in the whipped topping.
Spread cream cheese mixture on half of the cookies, then top each with the remaining cookies to form a sandwich.
Wrap each cookie in foil and place in the freezer for 1 hour or until ready to eat.
hints: Place the cream cheese mixture in a plastic bag, snip off one tip, and pipe the filling onto the cookie.

title: Lemon Blueberry Muffins
description: DaVita dietitian Heather shares one of her family’s favorite recipes, lemon blueberry muffins. She’s modified the recipe to reduce phosphorus and sodium making it kidney-friendly, while maintaining the flavor of comforting, old-fashioned cooking.
ingredients: 1 cup Rice Dream® rice beverage, original (unenriched)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Combine flour, baking powder and sugar in mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, combine egg, Rice Dream®, vegetable oil and lemon zest.
Pour liquid ingredients into flour mixture. Mix ingredients lightly until moistened; do not over mix.
Gently fold blueberries into batter.
Lightly spray 12 muffin tins with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon batter into muffin tins.
Bake for 25 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
hints: An alternative to spraying muffin tin with cooking spray is to line tins with muffin paper cups.
Freeze extra muffins then microwave for 30 seconds to serve later.

title: Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing
description: Looking for a dressing that’s thick and delicious? Try the kidney-friendly recipe Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing on the next salad you make.
steps: Mince garlic clove.
Combine all dressing ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.
Pour into a salad dressing flask. Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Use lemon juice instead of lime juice if desired.
Dressing keeps for up to one week in the refrigerator.

title: Basic Dressing
description: Learn how to make a basic, tasty, kidney-friendly dressing that works with almost any salad.
steps: Chop parsley and oregano.
Mix ingredients together to make 1/2 cup basic salad dressing.
hints: Try recipe with basil, dill, rosemary, or tarragon.
Substitute 1 teaspoon dried herbs if fresh herbs are unavailable.
Different flavored oils and vinegars also add variety. Try garlic oil, basil oil, or a small amount of sesame oil. For vinegar, try unseasoned rice vinegar or balsamic vinegar.

title: Citrus Salmon
description: Everyone knows that salmon is one food that’s really good for you. Now DaVita renal dietitian Jennifer from Wisconsin offers up her take on grilled salmon with a fresh lemon dressing spiced with cayenne, Dijon mustard, garlic and capers, plus a touch of basil and dill. Citrus Salmon is an easy-fix entrée that’s tasty and kidney-friendly to boot!
steps: Crush the garlic.
In a small saucepan, combine all the ingredients except the salmon. Heat to a boil, and then reduce the temperature to low and cook for 5 more minutes.

Meanwhile, preheat grill. Place the salmon, skin side down, on a sheet of foil slightly larger than the fish. Fold up the edges so the sauce stays with the salmon on the grill. Place the foil and fish on the grill. Top the salmon with the sauce prepared above.
Cover the grill and cook for 12 minutes or until salmon is cooked. (Do not flip salmon). Cut the salmon into 6 servings.
hints: Recipe was calculated with farmed Atlantic salmon. Wild Alaskan salmon is slightly lower in fat and slightly higher in potassium and phosphorus. Both are acceptable healthy choices for a kidney diet.
You can also cook this recipe in the oven at 350°F for 10 to 15 minutes until done. A good rule of thumb is to allow 10 minutes for each inch of fillet thickness.
If you are on a lower protein diet adjust portion to match your meal plan.

title: Dessert Cups with Fresh Fruit
description: Four kinds of fresh berries, phyllo dough and nondairy whipped topping are the only ingredients in Dessert Cups with Fresh Fruits. Simple, low in phosphorus, potassium and sodium and yummy!
ingredients: 3 cups Cool Whip® frozen dessert topping
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Spray 12-cup muffin pan with butter flavored Pam® cooking spray.
Layer 4 sheets of phyllo dough together, lightly spraying with cooking spray between each layer. Cut phyllo dough into 3-1/2″ squares and place in muffin pan to make dessert cups.
Place muffin pan in oven and bake 10-12 minutes or until phyllo cups are lightly browned. Cool to room temperature.
When ready to serve, fill each phyllo dessert cup with 1/3 cup fresh berries. Top with 1/4 cup Cool Whip dessert topping.
hints: If fresh berries are unavailable, use unsweetened frozen berries instead.
Sweeten fruit with sugar or sugar substitute, if more sweetness is desired.

title: Low Sodium Chicken Soup
description: When you have a craving for a warm and tasty light meal, look no further than the kidney-friendly recipe for Low Sodium Chicken Soup.
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast, boneless, skinless, cooked
steps: Dice chicken and set aside. Chop onion, celery and parsley; slice carrots 1/2-inch thick.
Sauté butter and onion in a 4-quart pot for 5 minutes, until tender.
Add water and chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add chicken, celery, parsley and pepper, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add carrots, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add frozen vegetables, cover and simmer 20 minutes longer.
hints: Look for reduced sodium broth containing 500 milligrams sodium or less per 1 cup serving. Avoid low sodium broths and bouillons containing potassium chloride—it’s very high in potassium. Recommended brands include Health Valley No Salt, Fat Free Chicken Broth (800-423-4846), Kitchen Basics Natural Chicken Stock and Swanson 50% Less Sodium Chicken Broth.
If you are on hemodialysis or restricted fluid, be sure to count liquid in the soup as part of your fluid allowance for the day.

title: Grill Thyme Corn on the Cob
description: Spice up your next cookout with Grill Thyme Corn on the Cob from DaVita renal dietitian Maria from North Carolina. A combination of thyme, black pepper and a spoon of Parmesan cheese add big flavor and keep sodium low in this summertime favorite!
ingredients: 4 half-ear size frozen corn on the cob
steps: Mix the oil, cheese, thyme and black pepper in a shallow bowl.
Place the corn in the oil mixture and roll to thoroughly coat corn.
Place all four pieces of the corn in the center of a heavy duty aluminum foil sheet. Pour any oil left in the bowl over the corn. Top the corn with 2 ice cubes.
Double fold the top and ends of the foil to make a packet, leaving room for heat to circulate.
Place the foil packet on the grill over medium heat and cook 20 minutes, turning once during cooking.
hints: Compared to most vegetables, corn is higher in phosphorus. A 1/2 ear portion is acceptable for a low phosphorus kidney diet.
Use fresh corn instead of frozen when in season.

title: Easy Egg Salad
description: DaVita dietitian Jennie has patients raving about her Easy Egg Salad recipe, and you are sure to love it too. Try it on a sandwich, on a salad or spread on low-sodium crackers for a high quality protein snack.
ingredients: 1/2 cup sweet onion (Vidalia® or other sweet onion)
1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® garlic & herb seasoning blend
steps: Hard boil the eggs for 8 minutes; turn the heat off and leave eggs in water for 2 additional minutes.
Peel the eggs and chop or grate to desired consistency.
Finely chop celery and onion. Drain pickle relish then measure 2 tablespoons.
In a medium bowl mix all ingredients together until well blended.
Chill at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving.
hints: If eggs are purchased at least a week ahead of time they will be much easier to peel when boiled.
Compare brands and select the mustard, mayonnaise and pickle relish with the lowest sodium content.
Refrigerate overnight for optimal flavor.
Serve with low-sodium crackers or spread on sandwich bread.
Keep egg salad in an insulated bag if taking away from home to keep it cold and avoid food spoilage.

title: German Pancakes
description: If it’s a different kind of pancake you’re craving, look no further than German Pancakes. The DaVita Dietitian Team came together to contribute this comforting breakfast dish for people with kidney disease.
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the flour and sugar. Add the eggs and blend well with a whisk.
Add the milk and vanilla extract. Beat until smooth.

Pour 3 tablespoons of the batter into a heated 8″ or 10″ nonstick skillet, sprayed with nonstick cooking spray. Tilt the pan quickly to spread the batter. Cook until the pancake is brown on underside (about 45 seconds; edges will begin to dry). Flip the pancake and brown the other side. Continue until all the batter is used.
Fold or roll thin pancakes and serve with fruit spread, jam or syrup. If desired, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of ricotta or cream cheese for a filling.
hints: If you have diabetes, use fruit spread or sugar-free syrup as topping.
Nutrient analysis does not include toppings. See chart below for selections.

title: Spaghetti Squash Stir-fry
description: Most varieties of winter squash are high in potassium. Spaghetti squash is one exception with only 180 mg potassium in one cup. But how do you prepare it? DaVita dietitian Susan shared her Spaghetti Squash Stir-fry recipe. It’s sure to be a hit with the whole family.
ingredients: 14 ounce bag classic slaw mixture with carrots
steps: Slice celery diagonally and dice onion. Set aside.

Wash spaghetti squash and pierce with a fork several times around the squash. Microwave on high for 2 minutes to soften. Cut the stem end off, cut in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds with membrane.
Place squash halves cut side down in a microwave safe dish. Put plastic wrap over the top with one corner vented. Microwave on high for 12 minutes. Cool and scoop out with a fork. Set aside.
Whisk together soy sauce, water, garlic, brown sugar, ginger paste, pepper. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add celery and onion, and cook until tender, approximately 3-4 minutes.
Add cabbage mix and stir until heated through, approximately 2-3 minutes.
Stir in spaghetti squash and soy sauce mixture until well combined, approximately 2 minute.
Serve immediately!
hints: If desired use 2 teaspoons fresh grated ginger instead of ginger paste.
Adjust portion to 1/2 cup for a lower potassium meal.

title: Sheet Pan Brussel Sprouts and Pears
description: Seasoned Cabbage Steaks add a new twist to this high-antioxidant cruciferous vegetable. Only 5 ingredients, and all you have to do is slice, season and bake.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F.
Remove the outside leaves of the Brussels sprouts. Cut in half. Cut the pears into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place 1 teaspoon olive oil in a mixing bowl. Add Brussels sprouts and toss to coat with the oil.
Transfer Brussels sprouts to a 9” x 13” pan and spread into a single layer on half of the pan. Bake for 12 minutes.
Place the remaining teaspoon olive oil in the mixing bowl. Add pears and toss to coat with oil.
Remove Brussels sprouts from the oven and add the pears to the other half of the pan. Roast for an additional 12 minutes, or until pears are tender.
Drizzle pears with 1 teaspoon balsamic vinegar glaze. Mix sprouts and pears together in a serving bowl.
hints: Balsamic vinegar glaze, also called balsamic vinegar reduction, may be purchased or made at home. For homemade, using a small saucepan bring 1 cup of vinegar to a boil then reduce to medium heat. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes until vinegar is reduced by half or until it reaches your desired consistency. Store extra in a covered container in the refrigerator.

title: Jellied Cranberry Sauce
description: Jellied Cranberry Sauce is a great reminder that you don’t have to wait for Thanksgiving to accent a dish with kidney-friendly cranberry sauce.
steps: In a medium saucepan combine sugar and 1 cup water; bring to a boil.
Add cranberries to water and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium and boil for 10 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Pour cooked cranberries into a wire mesh strainer over a mixing bowl. Using the back of a spoon mash berries to force pulp into the bowl. Discard skins.
Stir sauce and pour into a serving bowl. Cool at room temperature, then chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
hints: For a low sugar version use Splenda or other sugar-free sweetener.
Use frozen cranberries if fresh are not available.

title: Air Fryer Bagel Big Bites
description: This fun dish may bring a smile to your face. Serve with a greed salad and enjoy!
steps: Turn air fryer to 400 degrees F.
Arrange bagel thins cut side up, 4 thins total.
Dice the bell pepper into small pieces. Distribute marinara sauce amongst the bagel thins.
Distribute cheeses and pepper equally to bagel thins.
Bake in air fryer for 4-5 minutes.
hints: Can also be made in a regular oven at the same temperature, but increase the time to 10 minutes.
To make this gluten-free, Elyse used the brand O’Doughs Gluten Free Bagel Thins® (no phosphorus additives).
This recipe is a bit higher in sodium, so balance out your meals for the day. Look for bagel thins with the lowest amount of sodium per serving.
Use different colored bell pepper to change up the recipe.

title: Grilled Chicken Pesto Pizza
description: Pizza and chicken are two of the most popular dinner items. Now you can combine both with DaVita dietitian Amie’s kidney-friendly recipe for Grilled Chicken Pesto Pizza. Sun-dried tomato pesto combined with sautéed sweet peppers and onion replace the traditional red pizza sauce.
steps: Dice the bell peppers, onion and chives. Chop or shred the chicken.
Heat a tablespoon of olive oil and sauté the diced peppers and onion. Add the tomato pesto and cook for 2 minutes. Set aside for later.

Roll or stretch the pizza dough to a 10-inch circle or rectangular shape. Set on a floured, rimless pizza sheet or sheet pan (unless you are using an oiled grill pizza pan). Let sit for about 5 minutes.
Oil the grill surface and preheat the grill to hot heat.

Put pizza dough on the grill (no toppings yet), and grill for about 2 to 3 minutes. Check bottom for browning; bubbles will form on top. Reduce to medium-high heat if needed to prevent burning. When light brown marks are visible on the bottom of the pizza dough, take the dough off the grill and place pizza dough with grill marks up.
Top the pizza dough with the bell pepper, onion and pesto mixture. Top with the chicken, Romano cheese followed by the mozzarella cheese.
Place the pizza back on the well-oiled grill or grill pan. Grill for another 2 to 3 minutes, until cheese is melted and the bottom of pizza is browned.
Remove the pizza from the grill and garnish with chopped chives. Cut into 4 slices and serve.
hints: The sun-dried tomato pesto can be found in the produce section near the jars of minced garlic. If you are unable to find sun-dried tomato pesto, use 2 tablespoons sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil. Chop before mixing with the peppers and onions. Another alternative is to substitute 1/4 cup of pizza sauce.
A packet of active dry yeast is 0.25 ounces or about 2-1/4 teaspoons.
If you are not using a grill, use a grill pan or a large skillet and cook on the stove top. Can be cooked in the oven at 425º F.
Serve pizza with a tossed salad and low-sodium dressing.

title: Beef and Cheese Chile Rellenos
description: Chile peppers stuffed with two lower phosphorus soft cheeses are fried until golden. Try Beef and Cheese Chile Rellenos created by DaVita dietitians Cristina and Nana.
steps: Dice the onion and mince the garlic clove.
In either a hot skillet or directly onto the flame, heat chile peppers until skin is evenly blackened. Carefully, wrap chiles in plastic wrap or paper bag to continue to soften and cool.
Place 1 teaspoon oil, diced onion and garlic in a skillet over medium heat to soften. Add ground beef and cook until it crumbles and is brown. Set aside in a bowl.
Once chile peppers have cooled, peel off blackened skin and cut in half lengthwise. Remove the seeds and clean out the inside.
Add the asadero and ricotta cheeses to the cooled ground beef mixture. Stuff each chile half with this mixture.
In a small bowl beat the egg white.
Heat oil in a skillet. Coat each chile with a light layer of flour and then dip into the egg white to cover. Fry each chile in oil until golden.
hints: Run chiles under cold water to remove blackened skin.
Substitute poblano chiles or small bell peppers if Anaheim chiles are unavailable.
To reduce fat, reduce amount of cheese or eliminate. Use lean ground beef 7-10%.

title: Soft Ginger Cookies
description: The next batch of cookies from your oven should be the kidney-friendly recipe for Soft Ginger Cookies.
ingredients: 1/4 cup liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
In a medium bowl combine the flour, ginger, baking soda, cinnamon and cloves. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl beat butter with an electric mixer on medium speed for 30 seconds. Beat in 1 cup sugar.
Add liquid egg substitute and molasses; beat well.
Stir flour mixture into egg mixture.
Shape dough into 1-1/2″ balls, using about 1 heaping tablespoon of dough for each.
Roll balls in the remaining sugar to coat.
Place balls about 2-1/2″ apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes or until light brown and still puffed. (Do not over bake.)
Cool cookies on cookie sheet for 2 minutes then transfer cookies to a wire rack and let cool.
hints: If dough is too soft to handle refrigerate for 1/2 hour for easier handling.
Store cookies in a sealed container to keep soft.

title: Artichoke Relish on Toasted Pita
description: Artichoke Relish on Toasted Pita will give you crunchy satisfaction. Plus, it’s kidney-friendly, easy to make and good for people who have kidney disease, diabetes or are on dialysis.
serving_size: 2 tablespoons of relish on 2 pita wedges
steps: Drain and chop the artichoke hearts and pimento. Thinly slice the green onions and mince the garlic clove.
Combine all ingredients except the pitas in a bowl and mix well.
Cover and chill for 8 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350° F.
Split the pita rounds open. Cut each half into quarters, making 8 wedges.
Place the pita wedges on a baking sheet, smooth side down and spray with cooking spray. Bake for 8 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool the pita wedges and set aside in an airtight container until ready to serve.
Top each pita wedge with 1 tablespoon of Artichoke Relish.
hints: Bagel chips or pita chips work well too. Choose the lowest sodium chips.

title: Lentil Stuffed Peppers
description: Replace ground meat with lentils and brown rice for a high fiber, plant-based stuffed pepper dish.
ingredients: 8 ounces no salt added tomato sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F. Cut peppers in half vertically and remove ribs and seeds. Dice the onion and squash. Drain and rinse lentils and set aside.
Place cut peppers on a baking sheet, face down. Brush with 2 tablespoons olive oil and roast in oven for 15 minutes.
Place large pan over medium-high heat and drizzle in 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Add onion, squash and dried herbs; sauté 5 to 7 minutes until soft.
While onion and squash soften, chop garlic and add to pan; sauté an additional 2 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, broth and half the fresh basil leaves. Stir until basil wilts and all ingredients incorporated.
Add lentils and cooked rice and stir to combine.
Remove peppers from the oven, flip them and fill 1/2 cup lentil mixture into each pepper. Top each pepper half with 1 tablespoon feta cheese. Return to oven to bake an additional 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove from oven and garnish with remaining basil leaves.
hints: Lentil filling works great in lettuce wraps for an easy lunch.

title: Cucumber-Lemon Flavored Water
description: Water is one of the healthiest beverages for kidney patients–but nobody says it has to be plain and tasteless! Try Cucumber-Lemon Flavored Water, one of many flavored water recipes from DaVita dietitian Kara.
steps: Thinly slice cucumber and lemon.
Finely chop basil and mint leaves.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher.
Refrigerate overnight before serving.
hints: If desired, serve lemon and cucumber slices.
If you are on limited fluids, adjust the portion size to meet your needs.
After flavors develop you can pour into ice cube trays to make flavored ice.

title: Stuffed Strawberries
description: Lisa, a DaVita renal dietitian and former chef from New York, shares a delicious recipe for dessert. Lisa’s kidney-friendly dessert of Stuffed Strawberries is a sweet and healthy way to end a perfect day.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften. Rinse and remove stems from strawberries.
Place point down side up on a cutting board and cut a deep “x” in the top of each strawberry. Carefully spread berries apart.
In a small bowl, beat cream cheese and sour cream until smooth.
Pipe or spoon filling into each berry.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: Try stuffed strawberries at your next party or potluck. Your guests are sure to love this one.
Strawberries are a very low carbohydrate fruit. That’s why 4 large strawberries are counted as only 1/2 carbohydrate choice and only 1/2 serving of fruit.
One large strawberry is 1-3/8” diameter, not to be confused with extra large strawberries, 1-5/8” diameter. Twenty-four large strawberries is approximately one pound.

title: Dillicious Egg Salad Pita
description: When fresh dill is blended into egg salad it bumps up the flavor several notches. DaVita dietitian Vicky from Illinois named her recipe Dillicious Egg Salad Pita. That says it all!
steps: Cover the eggs with water in medium saucepan. Once the water is boiling, cover and turn the heat off.
Drain the eggs after 10 minutes. Cover with ice and water until cooled.
Peel the eggs and chop or grate to desired consistency. Chop the onion and dill weed.
In a medium bowl mix all the ingredients together until well blended.
Chill at least one hour in the refrigerator before serving.
Cut pitas in half and place 1/3 cup egg salad and 1/2 lettuce leaf in each pita half.
hints: For additional protein, Greek yogurt may be used in place of sour cream.
If fresh dill weed is unavailable substitute with 1 teaspoon dried dill weed.
If small pitas are not available serve with 1/2 of a large (6-1/2-inch) pita.
Serve on a lettuce leaf or with 6 low sodium crackers instead of pita if desired.
Keep this salad cold in an insulated bag if transporting to eat away from home.

title: Mojito Salsa
description: Fruit, cucumber, mint and lime juice are the main ingredients in Mojito Salsa. It’s great with low-sodium pita or tortilla chips, crackers or as a topping on meat or poultry.
steps: Wash and dice strawberries, cucumber and grapes. Dice watermelon. Shred mint leaves.
Combine fruit and cucumbers in a bowl. Zest the lime over the fruit. Cut the lime in half and juice into a small bowl. Add the honey and mix well.
Stir fruit with lime mixture, or if using a processor pulse until coarsely chopped. Mix in mint leaves.
Let salsa sit overnight in the refrigerator.
hints: Serve with low-sodium crackers or tortilla chips. Look for brands with the lowest amount of sodium.

You may also serve with homemade pita chips. Split the pitas in half and cut each half into quarters. Spray with cooking spray and bake at 350º F for about 8 minutes. You may also sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar after you spray with cooking spray.
Drain salsa through a fine sieve to remove fluid if you are on a fluid restriction.

title: Power Punch
description: We all need a pick-me-up from time to time, and a bubbly, refreshing kidney-friendly protein drink like Power Punch really hits the spot.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons sugar or sweetener of choice
steps: Blend cranberry-tangerine juice, whey powder, sweetener and ice in a blender till pink and frothy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.
hints: Ask your dietitian for more information about acceptable protein powders for kidney patients.
Sweeten to taste.
Serve with a swizzle stick of peppermint or a sprig of mint, if desired.
Juice may be substituted with Sunkist® regular or diet orange soda, cranberry, cranberry-raspberry or cranberry-grape juices.

title: Honey Butter Air Fried Salmon Filet
description: The salmon dish is a one dish meal. The sweetness of the honey lends a fancy twist to the salmon.
serving_size: 1 fillet, half of the vegetable mix
steps: Slice green onions, keeping white and green parts separate.
Cut cherry tomatoes in half, cut green beans in half if desired.
Pat salmon filets dry with a paper towel and season all over with 1 teaspoon black pepper.
Heat air fryer at 390 degrees F for 3 minutes.
Brush salmon with 1/2 tablespoon of olive oil. Air fry the filets for 11-13 minutes at 390 degrees F.
Mix butter, honey, and crushed red pepper in a bowl.
Remove salmon from air fryer to a plate and cover.
Mix green beans with 1/2 tablespoon olive oil. Air fry green beans 8-10 minutes at 390 degrees F.
Sauté cherry tomatoes and white portions of green onion in small pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
Place each salmon on a plate and spread honey butter over the top. Evenly distribute green beans, tomatoes and white green onion on the plates.
Sprinkle green tops of onion evenly on each plate.
hints: If you have diabetes, you may eliminate the honey butter and use only butter. Or you may eliminate the butter all together.

title: Curried Onion and Garlic Seasoning
description: Curry powder is the secret ingredient that sets this salt-free seasoning blend apart from other seasonings.
steps: Mix spices together in a small jar or bowl.
Store in a small jar or container for up to 6 months.
Use as an everyday seasoning in cooking and on entrees, vegetables and salads.
hints: Create your own personal seasoning blend by adding other spices such as oregano, cumin or dried lemon or lime peel.

title: Pancakes
description: There’s nothing more original than Pancakes, but this recipe is kidney-friendly. Enjoy a stack with other breakfast favorites today.
steps: Make sour milk: add 1 tablespoon vinegar to 2 cups milk. Let sit for about 5 minutes until soured.
Sift flour; add baking soda, salt and sugar.
Beat eggs with mixer until fluffy. Combine with “sour” milk and oil.
Add dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Cook on a hot griddle or heated frying pan, greased with nonstick cooking spray until bubbly. Turn only once for fluffy, light pancakes.
hints: Sour milk is used instead of buttermilk, which is higher in sodium.
The griddle must be hot. It is hot enough if a drop of batter sizzles.
Pour 1/4 cup batter for medium-sized pancake. Recipe makes 18 pancakes.
As soon as bubbles form, flip over.
This recipe is easy to cut in half. Leftover batter can be stored in sealed container for several days in refrigerator.

title: Sweet and Spicy Braised Beef
description: DaVita renal dietitian Johnna from Connecticut shares her kidney-friendly recipe for Sweet and Spicy Braised Beef, a satisfying main dish that’s easy to make with the help of your slow cooker.
ingredients: 12 ounces frozen apple juice concentrate, thawed
1 medium onion, thinly sliced into half moons
steps: Place sliced onion in slow cooker.
In large deep skillet, heat oil and brown beef on all sides.
Remove beef from skillet and place in slow cooker.
Add apple juice and spices to pan. Loosen browned bits from bottom of pan with spatula. Allow juice to simmer until reduced by approximately half.
Pour juice over beef in the slow cooker. Set slow cooker on low and cook for approximately 7 hours.
Remove beef from slow cooker to a deep platter or serving bowl. Shred using two forks.
Pour juice into a medium saucepan. Bring to simmer.
Wisk cornstarch into two tablespoons of water. Add to juice and cook until slightly thickened. If you would like a thicker sauce, simmer and reduce juice prior to adding cornstarch.
Pour sauce over meat and serve.
hints: Number of servings may vary depending on yield of meat.
This beef is delicious served in flour tortillas (think carne asada burrito) or on crusty rolls.
Serve with coleslaw or cucumber and onion salad.
Divide extra into portions and freeze for a quick meal later.
For a lower protein diet reduce portion size to match your meal plan

title: Roasted Turkey
description: The holidays are all about family, friends and food. And at the center of many holiday tables you’ll find a kidney-frienldy Roasted Turkey. The DaVita renal dietitian team offers this scrumptious recipe for Roasted Turkey flavored with fresh herbs. This delicious turkey is perfectly paired with the DaVita.com recipe for Fresh Herb Cranberry Stuffing.
ingredients: 12 pound turkey, fresh or frozen (avoid self-basting)
1 cup low-sodium turkey stock from turkey giblets
steps: Check plastic wrap on turkey to determine cooking time.
Preheat oven to 425º F. Remove neck and giblet bag from cavity of turkey. Rinse turkey with cold water, then pat dry with clean paper towels.

Using several fingers, loosen skin from turkey breast and drumsticks. Rub poultry seasoning onto turkey flesh under skin. Place parsley, sage, rosemary, and thyme sprigs between turkey skin and flesh.
Place a meat thermometer in the fleshy part of the thigh, without touching the bone.
Coat turkey with melted butter (or oil) and place breast side up in a roasting pan on a rack. Cover loosely with aluminum foil. Cook 30 minutes then reduce heat to 325º F.

Begin basting the turkey every 15 to 20 minutes with the giblet stock and pan juices. During last 30 minutes remove foil from roasting pan. Cook for 3 to 4 hours until meat thermometer registers 165º F.
Let turkey rest 30 minutes before carving.
hints: Three days before serving: if frozen, thaw turkey in refrigerator for 3 days. One day before serving: remove giblets from turkey and make giblet stock (see recipe).

Make the Fresh Herb Cranberry Stuffing if you wish to stuff the turkey. After step 3 above loosely place stuffing in the body cavity and neck. Use skewers and string to fasten neck skin under the body and tie legs together.
For CKD non-dialysis diet, please reduce serving size to match your meal plan.

title: Slow Cooker Leg of Lamb
description: Slow Cooker Leg of Lamb is seasoned with thyme, rosemary, black pepper, garlic and onion. Set the slow cooker on high for 5 to 6 hours and come home to dinner ready to eat.
serving_size: 4 oz. lamb, 1/2 cup vegetables and broth
ingredients: 2 cups low-sodium chicken stock or broth
steps: Trim excess fat off of the boneless leg of lamb and then place in the slow cooker.
Roughly chop the carrots, celery and onion. Finely chop the fresh rosemary and thyme.
Place all ingredients on top of lamb in the slow cooker and cover with lid.
Set slow cooker to high setting for 5 to 6 hours or until lamb is cooked through and can easily be pulled apart with a fork.
hints: Serve with rice or pasta for a complete meal.
Makes great leftovers, and freezes well.
If using low heat setting cook for 8 to 10 hours.
For a lower protein diet reduce lamb portion to 2 ounces.

title: Cranberry Chicken
description: Cranberries and mustard give a piquant “bite” to this sweet and saucy kidney-friendly chicken recipe by Jennifer from Maryland. Cranberry Chicken is a family favorite that Jennifer says was originally given to her mother and, “she’s been making it for years.” Tried and true, this dish is complimented best over a serving of white rice with a side of green beans.
serving_size: 1 chicken breast with 1/2 cup of sauce
steps: Chop onion.
Preheat oil in a large skillet. Add onion and sauté until clear.
Add chicken and cook for 3–4 minutes on each side.
In a medium-sized bowl combine ketchup, dry mustard, cranberry sauce, packed brown sugar and vinegar. Stir until mixed and pour into skillet.
Cover and cook on medium heat for 15–20 minutes.
hints: Serve with white rice and green beans for a complete kidney friendly meal.
Use Splenda® Brown Sugar Blend to reduce carbohydrate content if you have diabetes.
Another way to reduce carbohydrate is to substitute 1-1/2 cups of frozen cranberries in place of whole-berry cranberry sauce and add low calorie sweetener to desired sweetness.
For a lower sodium dish use no added salt ketchup without potassium chloride.
Cut large chicken breast-halves in half for 6 pieces.
Use chicken thighs or legs if you like dark-meat chicken.
Adjust the chicken portion to match your meal plan if you are on a lower protein diet.

title: Tuna Pasta Salad
description: DaVita dietitian Heather shares one of her family’s favorite recipes, Tuna Pasta Salad. She’s modified the recipes to reduce phosphorus and sodium making it kidney-friendly, while maintaining the flavor of comforting, old-fashioned cooking.
ingredients: 5 ounces canned low-sodium tuna in water
steps: Chop celery, bell pepper and green onion.
Combine cooked pasta, celery, bell pepper, onion and lemon zest in a mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together mayonnaise and salad dressing.
Pour dressing over pasta mixture.
Add tuna to pasta mixture.
Mix gently until all ingredients are moist and well blended.
Refrigerate one hour to let flavors blend.
hints: Macaroni can be substituted for bow-tie pasta.

Make low-sodium dressing using the Italian Dressing recipe on DaVita.com or shop for Italian dressing with lowest sodium content. Powdered dressing mix is a good choice because the sodium can be adjusted by using less of the mix.
If low-sodium tuna is unavailable, reduce sodium in regular tuna by rinsing for one minute.

title: High Protein Berry Shake
description: Here’s a great snack to help you add more protein to your dialysis diet. This delicious, high-protein berry shake features blueberries, but you can substitute strawberries, raspberries or blackberries for taste variations.
steps: Blend ingredients in a blender for 30 to 45 seconds.
Divide into two servings. Serve one now; freeze the second serving for later.
hints: Ask your dietitian to recommend an acceptable brand of protein powder.
For flavor variations try strawberries, raspberries or blackberries instead of blueberries.

title: Spicy BBQ Sauce
description: Spicy BBQ Sauce is a yummy and kidney-friendly recipe to use on chicken, beef and anything else that needs some extra zing.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons no salt added tomato paste
steps: Stir oil and flour together to make a paste.
Chop onion.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Cook the mixture on low heat until it thickens.
Brush sauce on baked or grilled meat.
hints: Kitchen Bouquet® is a browning and seasoning sauce composed of caramel with vegetable flavorings.

title: Shrimp Fried Rice
description: In the mood for some Chinese food tonight? Satisfy your craving with this authentic and tasty kidney-friendly recipe for Shrimp Fried Rice from DaVita dietitian Jennifer.
ingredients: 4 cups white long-grain rice, cooked and cooled
steps: Dice onion and chop scallions. Mince garlic and ginger root.
Preheat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper and cook until onion is tender, about 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and scallions and stir for about 1 minute.
Add shrimp and stir frequently until heated.
Add peas and carrots and stir until heated. Place shrimp and vegetable mixture into a large covered bowl.
Return skillet to the heat and add 2 tablespoons oil. Pour eggs into the skillet and scramble until done. Remove eggs to the bowl with shrimp and vegetables.
Return skillet to heat and add 1 tablespoon oil. Add 4 cups cooked rice and stir to heat and coat with oil.
Season rice with salt and pepper and let rice sit in skillet without stirring for about 2 minutes.
Stir rice and add the shrimp, vegetables and eggs. Serve hot.
hints: leftover chicken or 1/2-cup diced tofu for the shrimp
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or 1 teaspoon minced garlic for garlic clove
1/2 teaspoon ground ginger for fresh ginger
1 tablespoon reduced-sodium soy sauce for 1/4 teaspoon salt
2 scallions yield approximately 3 tablespoons chopped.
Jasmine rice adds extra flavor.
For a higher protein diet, increase shrimp.

title: Brewery Burger
description: DaVita dietitian Helen not only knows her way around the kitchen, but she can also tell you how to get around Colorado. Helen shares this delicious, kidney-friendly recipe for Brewery Burger and lays out a fun itinerary for visiting the Rocky Mountain state.
steps: Crush the soda crackers, then combine them with the milk in a bowl. Let stand until crackers are soft.
Beat the egg and stir into cracker mixture. Add the herb blend; mix well, breaking up the crackers if necessary. Add the ground beef and mix well.
Pat the ground beef mixture into 4 equal-size patties.
Grill over medium heat until cooked until the internal temperature is at least 160º F.
Serve on a bun with desired toppings, or serve patty with a vegetable and starch of choice.
hints: Always cook ground beef to a temperature of at least 160º F.
Nutrient analysis does not include bun, toppings or side dishes.

title: Shish Kebabs Lower Protein
description: Shish Kebabs are a quick and fun way get your protein and veggies, and they’re not just for summer barbecues. Dawn, a DaVita dietitian from Ohio, grills her kidney-friendly Shish Kebabs right in the oven.
steps: Combine the vinegar, oil, black pepper, garlic powder and oregano to make a marinade.
Cut the beef into 1-1/2″ cubes; Cut the onions into quarters; cut the bell peppers into 1-1/2″ squares.
Place the meat and vegetables in a covered container and marinade for at least 30 minutes.
Load the skewers, alternating meat and vegetables.
Grill the kebabs over medium heat for 10 to 30 minutes, depending on desired degree of doneness.
hints: Dawn uses sirloin steak for her Shish Kebabs, but you can use whatever meat you prefer.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 minutes prior to grilling to avoid burning them during the cooking process.

title: Easy Chicken and Pasta Dinner
description: Easy is a word most of us want to see on a new recipe. Chicken and pasta are two foods that combine to make a tasty meal. DaVita dialysis patient, Michael, came up with this delicious recipe for Easy Chicken and Pasta Dinner by adding red bell peppers, zucchini and low-sodium Italian dressing to the chicken and pasta to provide a zesty and hearty meal. This all-in-one dinner, submitted by DaVita renal dietitian, Mary Anne from California, is easy-to-prepare, kidney-friendly and mouthwatering.
serving_size: 1 cup pasta, 2-1/2 oz chicken, 2/3 cup vegetables
steps: In a nonstick skillet, heat olive oil and sauté zucchini and peppers until tender-crisp. Remove to a plate.
Cut chicken into strips.
Heat cooked pasta and chicken strips in microwave in separate dishes.
Toss pasta with Italian dressing. Top with chicken strips and sautéed vegetables.
hints: Do some pre-preparation to make this into a quick dinner. Cook a large pot of pasta, drain and refrigerate for use in this dish and other pasta dishes.
Broil or barbeque a pound of chicken breasts or thighs. Refrigerate and use for this recipe and other chicken dishes during the week.
If you require a lower protein diet adjust the portion of chicken in this dish.

title: Whipped Cream
description: Try making Whipped Cream at home to avoid phosphate additives and other unwanted ingredients. It’s so easy you may never buy already prepared whipped topping products again.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons sugar or sweetener of choice
steps: Place quart size bowl and mixers from a hand-mixer in the freezer for 15-20 minutes.
Pour whipping cream, vanilla extract and sugar into chilled bowl. Begin to beat on low speed. When cream begins to foam beat on high speed until stiff peaks are formed. Be careful not to overbeat.
hints: May use preferred sweetener to taste in recipe.
Use in recipes calling for whipped cream topping or Cool Whip® frozen dessert topping. Homemade whipped cream does not contain phosphate additives.

title: Protein Packed Bento Box
description: This bento lunch box makes a complete and easy lunch meal.
ingredients: One 4.5 ounce can tuna, no salt added, packed in water
steps: Drain tuna from can, and place in small mixing bowl. Dice celery and red onion.
Add mayonnaise, diced celery, diced onion, and spices to tuna bowl. Mix to combine.
Slice and skin cucumbers into spears. Slice apple into thin slices. Use 5 slices of cucumber from a medium cucumber for each box, if you are unable to find mini cucumbers.
Use two bento boxes. Put half he tuna mix, half of the carrots and half the cucumber to the boxes. Slice eggs in half and add 1 egg and 1 rice cake to each box.
hints: To make perfect hard-boiled eggs: add eggs to pan, and cover with water. Let water boil for 5 minutes, turn water off and leave egg in water for 10 minutes. Rinse in cool water, and peel immediately.
Instead of rice cakes, you may also use multi-grain crackers or corn thins. Stick to the serving on the box and look for lower sodium varieties.

This bento lunch box is a full meal. The potassium is higher than a normal entree, but it is considered a full meal and acceptable for a kidney friendly diet. Most of the potassium comes from fresh, natural foods.

title: Mojo Sauce
description: Jalapeno pepper, citrus juice, cilantro, cumin and oregano are combined with olive oil to make this popular Cuban Mojo Sauce. Try it with eggs or meat dishes.
steps: Remove seeds from the jalapeno pepper.
Place ingredients in a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
Store sauce in the refrigerator in a covered container for up to one week.
hints: Substitute parsley instead of cilantro if preferred. Replace jalapeno with your choice of chile pepper.
Adjust cumin and oregano to your taste.
Use Mojo Sauce as a marinade or dipping sauce. Try it with Sylvia’s Arroz a la Cubano recipe.

title: Pepper Steak
description: Pepper Steak is kidney-friendly and easy to make with Carol’s step-by-step cooking instructions. Simple, snappy and sensational!
ingredients: 3 pounds thin beef steak, cut into strips
2 cups green bell peppers, chopped fine
steps: In a large skillet brown meat in oil over medium high heat.
Add all vegetables and 1/4 cup water. Cover skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Add brown gravy mix and 1 cup water.
Stir over medium heat until thick.
hints: Compare brands and buy the lowest sodium gravy mix.

title: Pioneer Pumpkin Bread
description: This recipe makes 3 loaves of Pioneer Pumpkin Bread. Keep one and share or freeze the extra loaves.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Mix dry ingredients together in a large bowl. Add oil, water, eggs and pumpkin. Stir until well blended. Add nuts, if desired.
Pour batter into loaf pans, lightly sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
To makes 3 regular-sized loaves, bake for 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. To make 6 mini loaves, bake 45 minutes.
Cool loaves on a rack for 10 minutes in pans; then invert, remove from pans and turn right side up and continue cooling. Wrap in aluminum foil when totally cool.
hints: One cup chopped pecans (optional) added to this recipe increases potassium to 70 milligrams and phosphorus to 40 milligrams.
One cup walnuts (optional) added to this recipe will increase potassium to 86 milligrams and phosphorus to 57 milligrams.
Make loaves ahead and freeze until ready to share or enjoy.

title: Garden Vegetable Salad
description: DaVita renal dietitians from Minnesota share some of their favorite regional recipes that have been modified for the dialysis diet. By limiting phosphorus,potassium and sodium,dialysis patients can enjoy delicious Garden Vegetable Salad.
steps: Clean, wash and dry all vegetables
Coarsely chop lettuce and place into a salad bowl.
Slice cucumber and place on top of lettuce.
Chop or shred 4 baby carrots and place in salad bowl.
Cut or break apart broccoli florets into bite-size pieces.
Combine balsamic vinegar and olive oil and pour over salad.
Gently toss and serve.
hints: Low-sodium Italian dressing or another favorite salad dressing could be used in place of balsamic vinegar and olive oil.
A cooked chicken breast can be added to increase protein intake.

title: Arroz Con Leche (Rice with Milk)
description: Turn plain white rice into a yummy, kidney-friendly dessert with renal dietitian Melisa’s Arroz con Leche recipe. By substituting a low potassium, low phosphorus substitute for milk, dialysis patients can go back for seconds without exceeding their kidney diet goals.
steps: Rinse rice with tap water, then drain.
Add rice and 1 cup water to a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover with a lid and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove lid and stir in almond milk and raisins. Cover again and boil for 10 minutes or until the rice is well cooked. (Rice will have a soupy consistency; not all the liquid will boil off.)
When rice is done, remove from heat and stir in the sugar (or sugar substitute), cinnamon and vanilla. Mix well and serve warm.
Refrigerate leftover portions.
hints: Look for unrefrigerated almond milk and select a brand that does not contain phosphate additives.
Raisins are optional. Portion must be limited due to added potassium content.
Recipe was revised to eliminate nondairy creamer. Sugar was reduced from 1/2 cup to 1/4 cup. Adjust the amount if you like a sweeter dessert.
Carbohydrate choice is 2 when prepared with sugar substitute instead of sugar. Calories are decreased to 195 and carbohydrate to 27 grams per serving.

title: Florida Key Lime Pie
description: Graham cracker crust, lime juice, condensed sweet milk and whipped topping are the ingredients in Florida Key Lime Pie, a kidney-friendly treat from the DaVita dietitian team.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Melt butter and add graham cracker crumbs and sugar; mix thoroughly. Save 1 to 2 tablespoons crumb mixture to sprinkle on top of pie.
Press into a 9-inch pie shell. Bake for 5 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
In a mixing bowl add lime juice and condensed milk and mix thoroughly.
With a chilled bowl and chilled beaters, use hand-mixer to whip the heavy cream to a stiff peak. Fold the cream into the condensed milk mixture.
Pour mixture into the pie crust and sprinkle leftover crumb mixture on top.
Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Garnish with lime zest if desired.
This pie may be frozen for a frosty dessert.
This very rich dessert makes a wonderful occasional special treat. It is not recommended for people with diabetes due to the high carbohydrate and fat content.

title: Samosa
description: Savor the flavors of America’s melting pot with Tahseen, a DaVita renal dietitian from Florida. After living all over the world and sampling dishes from many cultures, Tahseen shares her recipes for Chinese Five Spice from China and Garam Masala from India. Today she shares a kidney-friendly recipe for Samosa, a popular snack from India that includes Garam Masala for low sodium seasoning.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons canola oil plus oil for deep frying
steps: Chop onion; finely chop ginger root and cilantro. Set green peas out to thaw.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large skillet, over medium heat. Add onion, ginger root, coriander, pepper and Garam Masala.
Add the ground beef and cook until it is no longer pink. Drain fat.
Add green peas and cook until the mixture is dry. Add cilantro and stir.
Mix 1 tablespoon of flour with enough water to make a thin paste.
Roll out pastry on a floured board. Put 2 tablespoons of the beef mixture in the center of the pastry and fold over. Seal edges with a paste of flour and water.
Heat oil for deep frying and fry pastries until golden brown.
hints: Egg roll wrappers or filo dough can be used instead of spring roll pastry if desired.
For a lower fat version you can bake the Samosa on a greased baking sheet instead of frying.
Instead of beef try ground turkey for variety.

title: Pineapple and Pepper Curry
description: Pineapple and Pepper Curry is a tasty low sodium side dish from Davita dietitian Rupa from New Jersey.
ingredients: 1/2 cup pineapple tidbits, canned in juice
steps: Chop bell pepper, onion, and cilantro. Cut cherry tomatoes in half. Shred ginger root.
Heat oil and when hot add ginger and red onion. Cook until onion is transparent.
Microwave peppers on high for 6 minutes. Add the peppers to onion mixture. Close the lid of the pan and cook on low for 10 minutes, stirring to avoid burning peppers.
Add pineapple tidbits and simmer for 2 minutes. Add curry powder and cilantro. Turn the vegetables once and let simmer on low for 2 minutes.
Garnish with cherry tomatoes and lemon juice before serving.
hints: Serve curry with bread or rice.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
description: Chicken Pot Pie is a classic, kidney-friendly recipe that will be at your dinner table more than once.
steps: In a large saucepan, place chicken, water and seasonings. Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.

Place diced potatoes in a large pot of room temperature water and bring to a boil. remove from heat, drain water and add fresh room temperature water. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Skim fat from broth.
Add carrots, celery and onion to broth and heat to boiling. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in boiled potatoes, parsley and bows and boil 14 minutes or until bows are tender.
Cut chicken into pieces and stir into pot pie mixture; heat through and serve.
hints: Farfelle pasta is also known as pot pie bows.
The potatoes are double cooked to remove part of the potassium. If you are not on a low potassium diet you can skip this step.
Freeze leftovers in individual portions for a quick meal later.
You can reduce the chicken to 1 pound if you are on a lower protein diet.

title: Pineapple Bread
description: Crushed pineapple and maraschino cherries are the star ingredients in this simply delicious Pineapple Bread.
steps: Set butter out to soften. Drain the pineapple. Chop the cherries.
With a mixer, beat sugar and butter until light and fluffy. Add eggs and mix well.
Mix flour and baking powder together.
Combine sugar and flour mixtures and blend. Add pineapple and cherries and mix to combine. Pour into a greased 9 x 5-inch pan. Bake at 350° F for 1 hour.
Cool for 10 minutes, then remove loaf from pan and transfer to a wire rack to cool. Cut into 15 slices.
hints: Make extra loaves and freeze until ready to share or enjoy.
To reduce carbohydrates use a granular sugar substitute.

title: Triple Berry Salad with Cottage Cheese
description: A healthy serving of food containing antioxidants can be like putting an invisible, protective shield in your system! And if you do this regularly, according to a smart food plan, the benefits will really pay off healthwise. Michelle K. from California makes it easy and delicious with her kidney-friendly recipe, Triple Berry Salad with Cottage Cheese.
serving_size: 1/2 cup cottage cheese and 1 cup berry mixture
steps: Wash all berries well.
Slice strawberries and combine with remaining berries in a bowl.
Add lemon juice.
Place cottage cheese on a serving plate or bowl, then top with berries.
Sprinkle with ground cinnamon (optional).
hints: Berries are a great source of antioxidants. Lemons are high in Vitamin C, and also a good source of antioxidants. Antioxidants help neutralize free radicals inside the body and keep cells healthy.

title: Spicy Lemon Pasta
description: Add some zest to your kidney diet with the kidney-friendly recipe for Spicy Lemon Pasta.
ingredients: 3/4 cup hot cooked whole wheat pasta
1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® onion herb seasoning
steps: Chop onion, celery and bell pepper.
Melt butter in a nonstick frying pan and sauté onion, celery, and green bell pepper. Stir into hot pasta.
Mix lemon juice, lemon zest, and Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning. Add to hot pasta and stir. Serve.
hints: Use pasta of choice. Cook according to package directions omitting salt.

title: Sweet Dijon-Glazed Turkey Breast
description: When you’re thinking of good protein sources, remember turkey. It’s a great change from chicken and beef, and DaVita renal dietitian, Maria from North Carolina, offers a tasty recipe for kidney-friendly Sweet Dijon-Glazed Turkey Breast.
steps: Wash turkey breast and prepare for roasting.
Place in a roasting pan, breast side up; cover and bake at 350° F for 1-1/2 hours (170° internal temperature using a meat thermometer).
In a small bowl, combine remaining ingredients and stir to blend.
Remove turkey breast from oven and brush glaze over top.
Return turkey to oven and cook uncovered for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven. Let turkey rest 15 minutes before slicing.
hints: Extra glaze can be served on the side as a dipping sauce.
Glaze can also be used on chicken.

CKD non-dialysis: This higher protein recipe may be appropriate for your diet if the portion size is adjusted to reduce protein content. Adjustments should be based on your individual protein prescription. Check with your dietitian if you are unsure.

title: Beef Brisket Gravy
description: Pass the gravy to add more flavor to your beef dishes. Beef Brisket Gravy is a kidney-friendly recipe that’s easy to make with either brisket pan drippings or low-sodium beef broth and a few other flavorings. For moist and delicious beef dishes, remember to make Beef Brisket Gravy.
ingredients: pan juices from cooked beef brisket
steps: Strain brisket pan juices and pour into a large measuring cup. Add water to make 2 cups broth.
In a small dish, combine 1/2 cup pan juice broth and flour. Whisk until smooth. Add remaining broth, vinegar and Worcestershire sauce.
In a medium saucepan, heat and stir broth over medium to medium-low heat until it thickens and comes to a rolling boil.
Remove from heat. Serve over cooked meat.
hints: Substitute 2 cups low-sodium broth if pan juices are unavailable.
A hot roast beef sandwich with beef brisket gravy makes a tasty lunch.
For smooth, lump-free gravy, stir flour into a small portion of broth before adding to heat.
Avoid heating gravy too quickly. Use medium-low to medium heat, and stir constantly as mixture starts to thicken.

title: Valentine’s Breakfast Eggs
description: You’ll be sweet on this DaVita kidney-friendly recipe, Valentine’s Breakfast Eggs.
ingredients: 2 slices of tomato, each slice 1/4” thick, chopped
steps: Place corn tortilla in the microwave for 1-1/2 to 2 minutes.
Crush tortilla into pieces, the size of chips.
Combine eggs and egg whites; scramble soft and set aside.
Put oil in a pan on medium heat and when hot, add onions and sauté 1 minute.
Add tortilla, tomato and eggs.
Stir until eggs are done. Serve hot and enjoy.
hints: Each microwave gives different cooking times, but you will know the corn tortilla is done when it smells like popcorn cooking.
Use 6 unsalted corn tortilla chips as a short cut.
Corn tortillas are high in phosphorus compared to flour tortillas or white bread. Limit corn tortillas to help reduce phosphorus, especially if your lab values have been higher than the normal range.

title: Golden Cornmeal Cookies
description: Suitable for those on diabetes, dialysis and CKD non-dialysis diets, Golden Cornmeal Cookies, crunchy, old-fashioned cookies are low in cholesterol, sodium, potassium and phosphorus.
ingredients: 1/2 cup liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Grease a baking sheet.
Sift the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt together into mixing bowl. Set aside.
In a separate mixing bowl, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg substitute and vanilla extract.
Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and beat until well blended.
Drop heaping teaspoons of the mixture onto the greased baking sheet in rows about 2″ apart.
Bake for 7 to 8 minutes until the cookies are golden brown at the edges. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.
hints: Use of liquid egg substitute instead of eggs helps lower phosphorus in this recipe. This is important in recipes that contain baking powder, a high phosphorus ingredient necessary for many bakery items.

title: Brie and Cranberry Chutney
description: A DaVita renal dietitian shares her Brie and Cranberry Chutney recipe for people who are on a kidney-friendly diet. People who have kidney disease, diabetes or are on dialysis can enjoy Brie and cranberry chutney found on DaVita.com.
serving_size: 3/4 ounce Brie, 2 teaspoons chutney and 3 low-sodium crackers
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Wash and drain fresh cranberries.
In a large skillet, heat water on medium for 5 minutes and add fresh cranberries. Heat for no more than 5 minutes, just until the cranberries start to burst.
Add white and brown sugar (or Splenda).
Add spices and stir gently.
Remove from heat. Let chutney cool.
Remove wheel of Brie from the wrapper. Leaving a half-inch border of rind on top of the wheel, cut out a circle and lift out rind from the center to expose the Brie inside.
Place Brie on a baking sheet and heat in oven just until the cheese is soft to the touch and the top is slightly melted.
Remove Brie from oven and place on a platter.
Pour warm chutney over Brie and serve with a variety of low-sodium crackers.
hints: Fresh cranberries are sold in 12 ounce bags.
Low-sodium crackers are recommended to help keep sodium low.
Substitute 1/2 cup Splenda® granular and1/4 cup Splenda® brown sugar blend for sugars. Substitutions reduce carbohydrate to 19 grams per serving, 1 carbohydrate choice.
Cranberry Chutney can be prepared and refrigerated for three days prior to serving.
Cranberry Chutney is a delicious side dish with turkey or lamb, or spread it on a turkey sandwich for a yummy flavor.

title: Cilantro Chutney
description: Cilantro Chutney is a refreshing item for snacks or as a spread for your sandwiches, and was developed by the mother of a DaVita dialysis patient and submitted by a DaVita renal dietitian.
steps: Wash cilantro and green chili.
Roughly chop onion, garlic, cilantro and chili.
Grind in a blender along with salt, cumin and lemon juice.
Serve with idli, on a veggie sandwich or with other snacks.
hints: Instead of 2 cups of cilantro, use 2/3 cup cilantro and 1/3 cup of mint for a sweet flavor.
One bunch of cilantro is approximately 2 cups.
Adjust chili for desired heat.
Decrease serving size to a teaspoon if used with a snack or 1 tablespoon if used as a sandwich spread.

title: Vegetarian Egg Fried Rice
description: June from Florida knows her dialysis patients crave Chinese fried rice from time to time, so she put her talents to work on a recipe for Vegetarian Egg Fried Rice that’s lower in sodium, potassium and phosphorus so it’s dialysis-diet friendly. Using basmati rice with extra firm tofu, egg, garlic, ginger and veggies provides authentic flavor and texture. While you are in the kitchen cooking up this recipe, remember that Confucius said, “It doesn’t matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.”
steps: Mince garlic and ginger root. Slice carrots. Dice yellow onion and tofu. Chop cilantro and green onions.
Beat eggs then sauté in a skillet like an omelet. Chop cooked eggs into pieces and set aside.
Heat oil in skillet over moderate heat. Stir in garlic, ginger, carrots, yellow onion, tofu, peas, and dry mustard.
When carrots are softened, add rice, chopped eggs and soy sauce. Mix, and turn off heat.
Stir in cilantro and green onions.
hints: Basmati rice has a better glycemic profile than other types of white rice. It is also lower in phosphorus than brown rice.
To reduce cholesterol you can use 1-1/2 cups low-cholesterol egg substitute to replace the 6 eggs.

title: Beef Tibs
description: Beef Tibbs, a popular Ethiopian dish made of spicy beef, is juicy and delicious. In its traditional form, it’s not very kidney-friendly, but DaVita renal dietitian Hanna from Maryland has adapted Beef Tibbs so that people on dialysis can enjoy it.
steps: Thinly slice onion. Chop tomato and bell pepper. Cut beef into small cubes.
Sauté onion and oil in a skillet until the onion is slightly brown. Add beef and tomatoes.
When partially cooked, add bell pepper, salt and pepper.
Continue cooking until meat is tender.
hints: Tibbs is a common Ethiopian dish that can be served with pita bread, half of a piece of injera or 1-cup cooked rice.
Variations of Beef Tibbs can be prepared by adding different ingredients of your choice.
Add 1 jalapeño pepper if spicier taste is preferred..
By using only a small portion of tomato, Beef Tibbs becomes an appropriate dish for dialysis patients.
Adjust the portion for a lower protein CKD-non-dialysis diet.

title: Creamy Cucumber Spread
description: A DaVita dietitian from Alabama shares a light and refreshing appetizer that’s perfect to beat the heat. Creamy Cucumber Spread will make your mouth water. It’s kidney-friendly, easy to make and good for home or a picnic at the park or on the beach.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften.
Peel, seed and finely mince cucumber and set aside. Mince onion.
Mix cream cheese, onion and mayonnaise in a small bowl and blend until smooth.
Fold cucumber into mixture until evenly blended.
hints: Low-fat or fat-free cream cheese works great, too.
Creamy Cucumber Spread makes delightful finger sandwiches. Cut the crust off bread and cut sandwiches into triangles for fancy appetizers.
This recipe is good on low-salt saltine crackers.

title: Chicken Pesto on Ciabatta Rolls
description: Chicken Pesto on Ciabatta Rolls is not your typical chicken salad sandwich. Basil-based pesto with chewy ciabatta rolls definitely kick up the flavor for this kidney-friendly sandwich.
steps: In a medium bowl combine shredded chicken, pesto, Greek yogurt and black pepper.
Slice and toast the ciabatta rolls.
Divide the chicken pesto mixture in half and make sandwiches with the rolls. Add shredded lettuce as desired.
hints: Use chopped arugula instead of lettuce if desired. Nutrients are similar.
For a lower protein sandwich cut chicken pesto mixture ingredients in half. Protein content is approximately 21 grams per sandwich.
To reduce carbohydrates serve on half of a mini-baguette instead of the ciabatta roll. Carbohydrate is reduced to 26 grams.

title: Crunchy Cornbread Salad
description: Crunchy Cornbread Salad was created by DaVita renal dietitian, Sara from California. She had leftover cornbread from her Southern-style Cornbread recipe and found it added a ton of great flavor to a salad.
